chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in the Muhrim changing his clothes, but when he enters Mecca he should wear the two garments of his Ihram in which he entered the state of Ihram, and it is disliked that he sell them.' And it is not permissible for the Muhrim to wash his garment unless something that necessitates its removal touches him. He narrated that.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.كُرِهَ: Disliked (recommended to avoid but not forbidden)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for wearing and maintaining Ihram garments during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical jurisprudence of Ihram, emphasizing the continuity of the sacred state by discouraging the sale of the specific garments worn during the ritual entry into Mecca. It further refines the legal boundaries of purity, permitting the washing of Ihram clothes only when impurity (najis) requires their removal, thereby balancing ritual integrity with practical hygiene. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly focus on maintaining the sanctity of the pilgrim's attire as a symbol of their consecrated status.
